newsitem.title: USA: Canada's surging gas exports pressure U.S. market.
newsitem.headline: Canada's surging gas exports pressure U.S. market.

text.p: A rising tide of Canadian gas exports is changing the competitive dynamics in the U.S. marketplace and a host of new pipeline projects promises to heighten the rivalry, gas industry sources said Thursday.
Canadian producers, long plagued by low gas prices, are eyeing several new projects that could dramatically increase deliverability to a more lucrative U.S. market.

"In the old days, there wasn't that much gas coming from Canada, but it has grown rapidly in recent years," Richard Hare, president of National Fuel Gas Supply Corp, said at the American Gas Association Bankers Conference here.
Hare said Canadian imports to the U.S. this year should average about 7.7 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd), nearly double the 3.97 bcfd exported in 1990.
And proposed export projects totaling some 3.1 bcfd promise to keep the competitive heat on U.S. producers to maintain market share.

"Canadian producers have been frustrated by low wellhead prices, so they want some of the action in the U.S.," Hare said, adding increased competition was likely to keep pressure on U.S. gas prices for some time.

He said expansion lines to the Midwest, like the Alliance and Northern Border projects to Chicago could back out some U.S. Midcontinent production, while projects to New England like Sable Island promise more competition for U.S. Gulf gas.

U.S. producers in the Rocky Mountain region have already felt the brunt of Canadian competition from increased capacity to the rich California market, with prices there generally well below the U.S. average.
"U.S. and Canadian producers will continue to compete aggressively at the major market area hubs," Hare said.
But he said rising competition and cheap gas prices should promote new markets in the U.S., possibly even displacing some coal in electricity generation.
Coal currently accounts for about half of all power generation in the United States.
